evidence: Agent image: task/environment/Dockerfile is byte-identical to the frozen template and builds from the environment/ context only, copying just instructions/ (conversations.md, integration.md, walls-and-retention.md) and assets/seed_data.json; it installs only express/better-sqlite3 globally (no rewardkit, no claude-code/codex judge client, no Playwright MCP) and /app starts from a single .gitkeep commit. grep for rubric|criteri|judge|reward|score|weight across instruction.md, instructions/*.md and seed_data.json finds no rubric content (seed keys: clock, firm, accounts, timer_options_days, matters, read_up_to); tests/, solution/ and app_context.md are not in the build context. Verifier isolation: task.toml:28 environment_mode="separate" with artifacts [/app,/assets] only; tests/Dockerfile (template-identical) installs rewardkit/claude-code/Playwright there, COPY . /tests then chmod -R go-rwx /tests. tests/test.sh (template-identical) sets umask 077 (l.3), chmod 700 $LOG_DIR (l.11), re-applies go-rwx on /tests (l.12), writes zero reward first, refuses symlinks outside node_modules, and launches the submitted app with env -i and setpriv uid/gid 65534 (l.104-110, restart helper l.160-166), so the agent-authored server cannot read /tests prompts/criteria, cannot see OPENROUTER/ANTHROPIC tokens, and cannot write reward.txt/reward.json, which only root-run score.py writes. The restart helper sits in the root-only 700 LOG_DIR. Adversarial tries: (a) agent planting a rubric-aware file or a symlink in /app to reach /tests -> rejected by the symlink scan and by root-only perms; hardlinks impossible across separate containers. (b) app reading criteria at grading time: rewardkit 0.1.7 ClaudeCodeCLI passes the prompt as argv to `claude -p`, so a uid-65534 process could in principle read /proc/<pid>/cmdline of the judge in the shared verifier container; this happens only during grading after the agent phase ends, cannot change reward files, and is a property of the shared template/RewardKit harness (both files byte-identical to template), not a task-specific defect - recorded as an observation, not a Fail. Conforming alternative: an app that writes logs to HOME/tmp works since HOME=/tmp/submission is nobody-owned; isolation does not penalize it. Static inspection only; no Docker run was needed for this row.
